A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Prediction-Powered E-Values and contain readable main text, equations, figures and complete Appendices A–C. Full-text and rendered-page comparisons establish no material gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on diabetes prevalence estimation, forest-cover risk monitoring, change-point detection and synthetic causal discovery in Sections 3.1–3.4 and Figures 1–4.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original empirical results in Sections 3.1–3.4 and Figures 1–4.

M1.justification: Section 2, Algorithm 1 and Appendix B.2 retain the identical prediction-powered e-value construction, model updates and data-collection procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same CDC diabetes survey data, Covertype risk-monitoring and change-point scenarios, and synthetic six-node causal graphs (Section 3; Appendix C).

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in every experiment, including labelled-only, imputation and vanilla PPI comparisons in Section 3.1, and labelled-only and full-data comparisons in Section 3.4.

E3.justification: Reported splits, metrics, poisoning procedures and budgets are identical. These include the 1% diabetes labelling budget, 0.5% risk-monitoring budget, and causal-discovery budget of 10% with batch size 100.

E4.justification: The active-versus-fixed sampling comparisons, poisoned/unpoisoned risk scenarios and case studies are unchanged. No ablation, robustness test or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Confidence-interval and hypothesis-test reporting is identical, including the displayed 95% intervals. No run counts, seeds, uncertainty estimates or significance analyses are added or revised.

E6.justification: Figures 1–4 and their result descriptions are identical, including confidence intervals, risk trajectories, detected change points and recovered causal edges. No numerical or qualitative findings change.

T1.justification: Section 2 and Appendices A–B preserve the same definitions, assumptions, theorems, proofs and derivations, including the asymptotic extension and approximate collection-probability optimization.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain identical claims about converting e-value-based inference into prediction-powered procedures, preserving validity properties and reducing data-acquisition costs.

C2.justification: Efficiency explanations and applicability qualifications are unchanged, including boundedness requirements, asymptotic assumptions for causal testing, and difficulties obtaining general confidence-set size bounds in Appendix A.

D1.justification: Implementation and data-processing disclosures in Section 3 and Appendix C, and the access links, are unchanged. The added funding acknowledgement supplies no technical or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The bibliography and positioning relative to earlier research are identical. References reflow after the acknowledgement, but no cited work is added or removed.

P1.justification: v2 adds an Acknowledgements section naming Canada's IDRC, Grant No. 109981, and UK International Development, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Scientific prose and organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The acknowledgement shifts references across columns and pages 9–10. Figures 1–4, Algorithm 1, equations and appendix layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 adds funding attribution but leaves the scientific content, evidence, explanations and reproducibility information unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. The acknowledgement and accompanying reference reflow do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
